governance.decisionForum: King’s Edge Portfolio Board, with the team’s organisational, workforce and professional-practice arrangements governed through the relevant Digital and IT forums.
governance.decisionScope: Material decisions about the team’s remit; the four funded experienced core posts, their planning grades, individual multi-year costs, final grades, start dates, future pay-award implications and planned transition into recurrent Digital and IT establishment from July 2029; the recurrent funding and workforce route for that 4.0 FTE BAU core; the planned one-year Junior Full-Stack sandwich placement in each of Years Two and Three, including employment route, supervision and learning model; whether solution architecture is covered within the Senior Backend & Integration Engineer post or separately; the small protected Business Analysis and DevOps/platform allocations; the £90,000 annual agentic software-development tooling allowance across all three mobilisation years and its final commercial implementation; leadership and decision rights; demand intake and prioritisation; any material increase in Hub scope that would compete with the King’s Edge roadmap; product and delivery practices; interfaces with specialist Digital and IT functions; evidence-based decisions to expand beyond the four-post core plus planned junior placement; whether agentic tooling, the placement model or additional capacity should join the recurrent operating model; handover criteria; and enduring institutional ownership.
governance.businessAsUsualOwner: Digital and IT product development capability owner – named owner TBC
governance.businessAsUsualOwnershipNote: The capability is expected to sit within Digital and IT. The strategic BAU anchor is the original 4.0 FTE experienced core: 1.0 FTE Senior Backend & Integration Engineer, 1.0 FTE Middleweight Full-Stack Engineer, 1.0 FTE Product & Service Designer and 1.0 FTE QA Engineer. These posts are funded through the three-year mobilisation to June 2029 and are intended to transition into recurrent Digital and IT establishment from July 2029 rather than ending with the programme. In constant 2026 planning prices, the four-post core costs approximately £203,000 in 2026/27 for the eight-month November-to-June mobilisation period, then approximately £304,000 in each of 2027/28 and 2028/29, or approximately £811,000 across the three mobilisation years. The current indicative BAU staffing run-rate is therefore approximately £304,000 per year from 2029/30, before future pay awards and final appointment-point effects. This recurrent liability is recorded separately from mobilisation investment so it is visible without being double-counted. From Year Two, the experienced core is augmented by one 1.0 FTE Junior Full-Stack Engineer sandwich-year placement per year, with a £35,000 annual planning employment envelope. The placement remains a supervised capability and talent-pipeline test rather than part of the committed BAU core. Digital and IT / HR must validate final grades, appointment points, placement route, start dates and future pay awards. Mark Peace is Product Owner during mobilisation. The Product & Service Designer combines UX/UI, service design, prototyping and user research. Outside the funded team, the working assumption is deliberately lean: approximately 0.2 FTE protected Business Analysis during the main discovery period and approximately 0.2 FTE DevOps/platform support, with up to approximately 0.2 FTE solution architecture only if the senior engineering post cannot carry that function. Product quality assurance sits with the QA Engineer; specialist security, privacy, accessibility, data, architecture assurance and service-management input is drawn from existing institutional functions when required rather than represented as standing fractional posts. Ring-fenced agentic software-development tooling is profiled at £90,000 in each of the three mobilisation years, £270,000 total, while Digital and IT validates the exact commercial structure and whether shared capacity can reduce actual spend. The directly quantified 4.1.3 mobilisation profile is therefore approximately £293,000 in Year One and £429,000 in each of Years Two and Three, or approximately £1.151m across mobilisation before valuing existing shared capacity. The end-of-mobilisation question is not whether the four-post core survives: the planning assumption is that it transitions to BAU. The remaining decisions are the recurrent funding route, final organisational and professional leadership arrangements, and whether agentic tooling, the placement model or any additional capability also continue after June 2029.
